STEP 1 - Scene: Scrambled eggs on a white square plate, photographed from above (near top-down angle). It appears to be a breakfast-style single serving.

STEP 2 - Ruler: White square plate, roughly 22 cm across at its widest (the plate spans most of the frame width). Plate area ≈ 22 x 22 x ~0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 410 cm². Using a 3.14 x (diameter/2)² circle equivalent of ~22 cm gives ~380 cm²; I use ~400 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: Scrambled egg (yellow, soft curds), with small flecks of orange/red (likely finely diced pepper or carrot bits) and no visible oil pool.

STEP 4 - Area: Scrambled egg covers roughly 40% of the plate's surface (the pile sits in the center-right, not spreading to the edges). Egg ≈ 40% of 400 cm² ≈ 160 cm². Pepper/vegetable flecks are a negligible share, included within the egg area.

STEP 5 - Volume: Pile height averages ~2 cm (fluffy, irregular peaks). 160 cm² x 2 cm = 320 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Egg bulk density ~0.9 g/ml. 320 ml x 0.9 ≈ 288 g. Trimmed for the flecked, fluffy texture and the plate edges, I estimate ~250 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Scrambled egg, cooked, ~150 kcal per 100 g (typically made with some butter/milk). 250 g x 1.5 = ~375 kcal. Small vegetable bits add negligible energy.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A single generous serving of scrambled eggs (about 2–3 large eggs) weighs roughly 150–250 g and carries about 200–400 kcal. The estimate sits at the upper-middle of that range, which is plausible for a visible pile of this size. I'll take a slightly more conservative figure of ~220 g.

Adjusted: 220 g x 1.5 kcal/g ≈ 330 kcal.
